title: eSanjeevani
prompt: What would it take to speak to a specialist without losing a day’s wages?
workflow: In the assisted model, a community health officer connects a patient at a local health centre with a doctor at a hub. The local team can collect the history and help the patient use the service.
test: Give the local team an agreed route for an in-person visit when the remote clinician requests one. Assign someone to check whether that visit happened.
measure: Share of patients needing an in-person referral who complete it within the agreed interval.
balance: Compare travel time, repeat visits and completion for patients who need language or digital assistance.
discuss: If the specialist queue doubles, whose waiting time has the service actually saved?
source: MoHFW · Health and Family Welfare Statistics in India, 2023

title: Narayana Health’s Medha Scribe
prompt: When the note is ready sooner, who still has to check it before another clinician relies on it?
workflow: Narayana Health reports deploying Medha Scribe for clinical documentation in echocardiography and radiology. A draft changes how staff spend their time and where checking matters.
test: Observe a reporting session from dictation to sign-off. Give the reporting clinician a review step, capture material corrections and retire duplicate entry where feasible.
measure: Median staff minutes per signed report, counting drafting, checking and corrections.
balance: Audit material errors in signed reports and time spent by nurses or transcription staff on rework.
discuss: Which task can you remove from the old workflow on the day the new one goes live?

title: Delhi’s community TB screening
prompt: If a screening camp flags a result, can the person complete the next test before returning to work?
workflow: Delhi teams used portable chest X-rays with AI-assisted reading. Of 18,377 people with presumed TB, 16,866 completed molecular testing. That leaves 1,511 without a recorded molecular test in this group.
test: Interview people who missed testing. Trial a change such as same-visit sample collection, with the diagnostic team responsible for tracing outstanding samples.
measure: Molecular tests completed / people with presumed TB. The study reported 91.7%.
balance: Check coverage among eligible residents and time to treatment. The programme evaluation cannot isolate the contribution of AI.
discuss: For blood work, imaging and genetics, who explains a result that needs follow-up or further interpretation?
source: Saini et al. · Indian Journal of Tuberculosis, 2026

title: Aravind Eye Care System
prompt: Does the hospital know which patients from a local vision centre actually arrive?
workflow: In Aravind’s model, vision-centre staff examine patients and share findings with a hospital ophthalmologist by teleconsultation. Patients who need more advanced care can be referred to the base hospital.
test: Pair each referral with a receiving team, a feasible appointment and a way for the local centre to see the outcome. Investigate missed visits before expanding screening.
measure: Completed specialist visits / patients referred, within a stated follow-up window.
balance: Track time to appointment and travel cost. Check hospital capacity when referrals rise.
discuss: If you had funding for one more technician or one more specialist session, what data would decide it?
source: Aravind Eye Care System · Vision Centre Implementation Guidance

title: DawaiSaathi
prompt: At home after eye surgery, how do I recognise the right bottle when several drops are due?
workflow: Sachin Gaur described building a medication-reminder prototype after seeing the difficulty of managing eye-drop schedules in his family. Pictures and familiar voice instructions connect a written plan to a task at home.
test: Ask a caregiver to show how they follow the plan on a busy morning. Test how they distinguish bottles and how they learn that a clinician changed the schedule.
measure: In a supervised usability test, count tasks completed correctly / tasks attempted.
balance: Test with shared phones and without a phone. Check whether an outdated reminder persists after a schedule change.
discuss: What did observing the person at home reveal that a discharge form could never tell you?
source: First-hand account · Holy Family nursing panel, 19 November 2026

title: ABDM record sharing
prompt: How many times must I find my old report before the new doctor can use it?
workflow: India’s Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission specifies consent-based exchange between participating health information providers and users. A linked record can be requested and shared across systems.
test: At the next visit, test whether the team can locate the correct report in time. Provide assistance, a paper fallback and an auditable route to correct a mismatched record.
measure: Visits with the needed prior report available before the decision / visits needing that report.
balance: Compare success for people with a shared phone. Track wrong-record incidents, consent failures and downtime.
discuss: Who can retrieve what, for which purpose, and what does the clinic do during an outage?
source: National Health Authority · Health information provider and user guidelines

title: National Health Claims Exchange
prompt: After a clinician clears me to leave, who can tell me why the claim is waiting?
workflow: NHCX gives providers and payers a standard way to exchange claims-related information. An insurer or its administrator still assesses the request and returns a decision or query.
test: Separate time spent compiling evidence from time waiting for a payer. Assign staff to unresolved queries and give families a clear status update.
measure: Median and 90th-percentile time from complete submission to payer decision.
balance: Monitor denials, out-of-pocket charges and the interval from clinical discharge to departure. Also track days to payment.
discuss: If settlement accelerates but denials rise, whose financial position has improved?
source: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare · Update on NHCX

title: Rajasthan’s e-Aushadhi
prompt: When a kit is missing, who sees the cancelled test or extra visit it caused?
workflow: Rajasthan’s medical procurement agency uses e-Aushadhi to track stocks of drugs, sutures and surgical supplies. Its workflow includes reorder levels, expiry information and transfers between warehouses.
test: Trace one item from the warehouse to the room where it is used. Test whether a shortage report gives the storekeeper enough time to act before a patient’s visit.
measure: Count postponed procedures or tests attributable to a missing item per 100 scheduled.
balance: Track expiry waste and compare system balances with a physical count at the point of care.
discuss: Would you fund a bigger buffer, better recording of use or faster transfers? What observation would change your choice?
source: Rajasthan Medical Services Corporation · e-Aushadhi application

title: India’s Adverse Drug Monitoring System
prompt: If a patient reports a suspected reaction at home, who hears about it beyond the consultation?
workflow: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission’s ADRMS portal supports adverse-event reporting by patients, caregivers and health professionals. Pharmaceutical companies can submit reports through a dedicated gateway.
test: Walk through a suspected-reaction report with a pharmacist. Identify who checks completeness, who follows up and how the patient reaches their treating team for individual care.
measure: Share of reports with the information needed for assessment, and time to follow-up when requested.
balance: A rise in reporting can reflect better detection. Report counts alone cannot establish causality or incidence.
discuss: Which fields are essential for safety review, and which discourage reporters from finishing?

title: Dozee’s contactless ward monitor
prompt: When several beds generate alerts at once, how does the nurse decide whom to see first?
workflow: InnoHEALTH profiled the Indian company’s under-mattress sensor and its use for remote monitoring. It can capture signals such as heart rate and breathing rate between staff observations.
test: Shadow a ward team across a shift change. Agree who receives an alert, who checks the patient and who takes over if the assigned nurse is busy.
measure: Time from an actionable alert to bedside assessment, including nights and shift changes.
balance: Count alerts per occupied bed-day, alerts requiring no action, and escalations missed during downtime.
discuss: Would you add sensors to ten beds if you could not add anyone to respond at night?
source: InnoHEALTH Magazine · Innovation for hospitals during COVID-19
